verses.text: When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see, he called for Esau, his older son. "My son," he said. "Here I am," Esau answered.
Isaac said, "I am now an old man, and I do not know when I will die.
So get your weapons, your bow and arrows, and go out into the open country to hunt some wild animals for me.
Cook me the kind of tasty food I like and bring it to me to eat. Then I will give you my blessing before I die."
Now Rebekah was listening while Isaac spoke to his son Esau. When Esau left for the open country to hunt for wild meat and bring it back,
Rebekah said to her son Jacob, "Listen! I heard your father say to your brother Esau,
'Bring me some wild meat and cook me some tasty food to eat. Then I will bless you in front of the LORD before I die.'
Now, my son, listen carefully and do what I tell you.
Go out to the flock and bring me two of the best young goats. I will cook some tasty food for your father, just the way he likes it.
Then take it to your father to eat, so that he will give you his blessing before he dies."
Jacob said to his mother Rebekah, "But my brother Esau is a hairy man, and my skin is smooth.
What if my father touches me? He will see that I am tricking him, and I would bring a curse on myself instead of a blessing."
His mother said to him, "My son, let the curse fall on me. Just do what I say. Go and get the goats for me."
So he went and got them and brought them to his mother, and she cooked some tasty food, just the way his father liked it.
Then Rebekah took the best clothes of Esau, her older son, which she had in the house, and put them on her younger son Jacob.
She also covered his hands and the smooth part of his neck with the goatskins.
Then she handed her son Jacob the tasty food and the bread she had made.
He went to his father and said, "My father." "Yes, my son," he answered. "Who is it?"
Jacob said to his father, "I am Esau, your firstborn. I have done as you told me. Please sit up and eat some of my wild meat, so that you can give me your blessing."
Isaac asked his son, "How did you find it so quickly, my son?" He replied, "The LORD your God gave me success."
Then Isaac said to Jacob, "Come near so that I can touch you, my son, to know whether you really are my son Esau or not."
Jacob went close to his father Isaac, who touched him and said, "The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau."
He did not recognise him, because his hands were hairy like those of his brother Esau. So he got ready to bless him.
"Are you really my son Esau?" he asked. "I am," he replied.
Then Isaac said, "Bring me some of your wild meat to eat, my son, so that I can give you my blessing." Jacob brought it to him, and he ate. Then he brought him some wine, and he drank.
Then his father Isaac said to him, "Come here, my son, and kiss me."
So he went to him and kissed him. When Isaac smelled the smell of his clothes, he blessed him and said, "The smell of my son is like the smell of a field that the LORD has blessed.
May God give you dew from the sky and rich soil on the earth, and plenty of grain and new wine.

May nations serve you and peoples bow down to you. Be the master over your brothers, and may your mother's sons bow down to you. May those who curse you be cursed, and may those who bless you be blessed."
Isaac had just finished blessing Jacob, and Jacob had hardly left his father's presence, when his brother Esau came in from hunting.
He too cooked some tasty food and brought it to his father. Then he said to him, "My father, please sit up and eat some of my wild meat, so that you can give me your blessing."
His father Isaac asked him, "Who are you?" "I am your son," he answered, "your firstborn, Esau."
Isaac began to shake all over and said, "Then who was it that hunted wild meat and brought it to me? I ate it just before you came, and I blessed him. And he will be blessed!"
When Esau heard his father's words, he cried out loudly and bitterly. He said to his father, "Bless me too, my father!"
But Isaac said, "Your brother came and tricked me, and he has taken your blessing."

Esau said, "Is he not rightly named Jacob? He has cheated me two times now. He took my rights as the firstborn, and now he has taken my blessing!" Then he asked, "Have you not kept back any blessing for me?"
Isaac answered Esau, "I have made him master over you, and I have made all his relatives his servants. I have given him plenty of grain and new wine. So what can I possibly do for you, my son?"
Esau said to his father, "Do you have only one blessing, my father? Bless me too, my father!" And Esau wept loudly.
His father Isaac answered him, "You will live far away from the rich soil of the earth, far from the dew of the sky above.
You will live by the sword, and you will serve your brother. But when you grow restless, you will throw his heavy load off your neck."
Esau held a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing his father had given him. He said to himself, "The days of mourning for my father are near. Then I will kill my brother Jacob."
When Rebekah was told what her older son Esau had said, she sent for her younger son Jacob. She said to him, "Your brother Esau is comforting himself with the thought of killing you.
Now then, my son, do what I say. Run away at once to my brother Laban in Haran.
Stay with him for a while, until your brother's fury calms down.
When your brother is no longer angry with you and has forgotten what you did to him, I will send word for you to come back from there. Why should I lose both of you in one day?"

Then Rebekah said to Isaac, "I am sick and tired of my life because of these Hittite women. If Jacob marries one of the women of this land, a Hittite woman like these, my life will not be worth living."
